h1: Clef Hotel Samut Prakan — Clean Rooms with Balconies in the Samrong–Bearing Area Near BTS
intro: If you want a Samrong-area base with clean, well-kept rooms and easy BTS Green Line access into the city, Clef Hotel is a long-standing favourite that guests praise for cleanliness and service. This midrange, 89-room hotel sits on Soi Bearing 6, Sukhumvit 107, in Samrong Nuea, Mueang Samut Prakan — about 700 metres from BTS Bearing, with the Green Line running straight into central Bangkok. Rooms have private balconies, there's free parking, and the breakfast earns regular praise. Prices start from approx. ฿800/night, and it holds an 8.5 score from over 220 real guest reviews on Trip.com.

body.html: The reason guests come back to Clef Hotel is its consistent cleanliness and upkeep. Many reviews mention spotless rooms, comfortable beds and friendly, helpful staff. Rooms are comfortably sized for the price, with a fridge and minibar, and the detail many guests love is the private balcony in nearly every room — somewhere to catch the breeze and natural light, rather than the boxed-in feel of typical budget rooms.

The location is on Soi Bearing 6, Sukhumvit 107, in the Samrong Nuea area — about 700 metres from BTS Bearing and not far from BTS Samrong, both on the Green Line, running straight to Asok, Siam and on to On Nut. There are night markets, restaurants and convenience stores within walking distance. It's about a 25–30 minute drive to Suvarnabhumi Airport, so it works as a pre-flight base, though it isn't airport-adjacent like the Bang Phli hotels.

Facilities are appropriate for a midrange hotel. There's free parking, an on-site restaurant, a buffet breakfast (for a fee) and free Wi-Fi. The free parking is something self-drivers praise, since parking around the far end of Sukhumvit is scarce. The breakfast earns praise for taste and freshness, though some reviews note the spread isn't large — fine for a simple meal before heading out.
"The room was super clean, the staff were friendly, you can walk to BTS Bearing, and there's plenty to eat nearby. Great value and a tasty breakfast — we'll definitely stay again."

The thing to know up front is that there's no swimming pool. A few guests have been caught out because some platform descriptions wrongly mention a pool — but there isn't one, so if you want to swim, choose another hotel in this list. Beyond that, some reviews mention small issues like the shower or water pressure in certain rooms — worth checking at check-in and asking to switch if you're unhappy.

Another point to keep in mind is that this is a quiet, restful hotel down a side soi, not a hub of activity. There's no real gym or spa, and Soi Bearing 6 itself is fairly quiet — at night you may need to walk out to the main road to grab a ride or find food. The trade-off is calm and good sleep, away from the direct noise of Sukhumvit Road.

Overall, Clef Hotel holds an 8.5 out of 10 on Trip.com from over 220 real guest reviews — high for a hotel at this level. It's a sensible pick for travellers who want a clean room with a balcony, rely mainly on the BTS, or drive in and need free parking. Prices start around ฿800 and climb with the season into the mid-thousands for a suite. If you don't need a pool or full resort-style facilities, it offers solid value in the Samrong area.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Clef Hotel Samut Prakan

faq.q: Where is Clef Hotel, and is it near the BTS?
faq.a: The hotel is on Soi Bearing 6, Sukhumvit 107, in Samrong Nuea, Mueang Samut Prakan. It's about 700 metres from BTS Bearing (Green Line) — within walking distance — and not far from BTS Samrong. The Green Line runs straight to Asok and Siam. It's about a 25–30 minute drive to Suvarnabhumi Airport.

faq.q: How much does Clef Hotel cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start from approx. ฿800/night for a Studio Room. Options range from Supreme Rooms up to a Suite with a separate living area. Rates climb with the season into the mid-thousands — always compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: What are the rooms like at Clef Hotel — are they clean?
faq.a: The standout is consistent cleanliness and upkeep, the most praised point in reviews. Rooms are comfortably sized, with a fridge, minibar and a private balcony in nearly every room. A few reviews mention the shower or water pressure in some rooms, so it's worth checking at check-in.

faq.q: Does Clef Hotel have parking and a pool?
faq.a: There's free parking, which self-drivers praise, since parking around the far end of Sukhumvit is scarce. There's an on-site restaurant and a buffet breakfast for a fee. But there's no swimming pool (some platform descriptions list one incorrectly) — worth knowing if you're hoping to swim.

faq.q: Who is Clef Hotel best for?
faq.a: It suits travellers who want a clean room with a balcony and rely mainly on the BTS, or self-drivers who need free parking. It works for a quiet stay and an unhurried pre-Suvarnabhumi night, but it's less suited to anyone wanting a pool, gym or full resort-style facilities.

faq.q: How long is the drive from Clef Hotel to Suvarnabhumi Airport?
faq.a: It's about a 25–30 minute drive depending on traffic. The hotel has no dedicated airport shuttle, but taxis and Grab are easy to arrange. Because it isn't airport-adjacent like the Bang Phli hotels, allow enough travel time for very early flights.
